name: Kyoto
tagline: Temples at first light, gardens, and the discipline of doing less.
distinctive: Kyoto's temples, gardens and craft traditions are best met early in the morning and slowly. Its extraordinary architecture ranges from Zen gardens to the Katsura Imperial Villa.

image.alt: Yasaka Pagoda above a quiet lane of wooden houses in Kyoto

moodNotes.art: Ryōan-ji's rock garden, the Katsura Imperial Villa and a living tradition of craft.
moodNotes.lifetime: Kyoto at dawn, before the city wakes, is one of travel's great quiet experiences.
moodNotes.wellness: Gardens, tea, forest walks and hot springs a short drive north set a calm pace.
moodNotes.city: The lantern-lit lanes of Gion and a long kaiseki dinner make the evenings.
moodNotes.weekend: Long-haul from most departure points. It needs more than a weekend.

seasonNote: Cherry blossom (usually early April) and autumn colour (usually November) are beautiful and very busy. Summer is hot and humid.

arrival.transfer: From Kansai International, the Haruka limited express reaches Kyoto Station in roughly 75–80 minutes. A private car takes about 90 minutes or more, depending on traffic.
arrival.groundNote: Arriving via Tokyo, the Shinkansen to Kyoto takes a little over two hours.

driving.note: Kyoto's streets are narrow and parking is scarce, and Japan requires an International Driving Permit. Rail, taxis and a private driver work far better.

transfer.label: Rail and a private driver
transfer.why: The train for the arrival, and a private driver for the scattered temples and gardens on the city's edges.

stay.name: Aman Kyoto
stay.why: A secluded retreat in a forest garden at the foot of Kyoto's northern hills, close to Kinkaku-ji and well placed for early temple visits.

watchWhy: The Snowflake's textured dial is inspired by snow in Japan, and its gliding Spring Drive seconds hand suits a city of patient craft.
aromaWhy: Hinoki, the cypress of Japanese baths and temples, with green tea and a thread of incense.

days.title: Northern temples
days.text: Visit Kinkaku-ji as it opens, then the rock garden at Ryōan-ji. Rest in the afternoon and have a kaiseki dinner in the evening.

days.title: The eastern hills
days.text: Reach Kiyomizu-dera early and walk down through Higashiyama. Join a tea ceremony in the afternoon, then walk the lanes of Gion at dusk.

days.title: Arashiyama and Katsura
days.text: See the bamboo grove at first light, then tour the Katsura Imperial Villa, which requires an advance reservation.

moreDays.title: Kurama and Kibune
moreDays.text: Walk the forest trail between the two mountain villages, with lunch by the stream in summer.

moreDays.title: Nara
moreDays.text: Take a day trip to Tōdai-ji and the deer park, arriving early.

moreDays.title: Miho Museum
moreDays.text: Drive into the Shiga hills to I. M. Pei's Miho Museum, as remarkable for its approach as its collection.
